Aisha — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We're on it. Quick summary so everyone has the latest:

- Initial signal shows dedicated GPU pool for VivaReso is at 96–98% occupancy and queue depth has tripled for short windows.
- Error pattern looks like token queue timeouts (gateway 5xx) — lower-level logs attached for ops triage.

Immediate next steps (we're executing now):
1) Ops (Irene + Priyom) will run a targeted slot-map check to see whether cross-tenant spillover is active and if any reclaimed burst capacity is available.
2) Marissa will prepare a customer-facing note with two fallback options: a) short-term traffic shaping + canary to smaller context model, b) provisional burst allocation (if procurement/credits approved).
3) I'll coordinate an exec-level heads-up and put this on the CTO/CSO rapid sync if we need cross-org procurement.

I'll share a concrete remediation timeline in the next 30–45 minutes.

—Sean Gallagher
Sr. Site Reliability Liaison, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-08-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (urgent) increased 5xx and latency from dedicated pool

Quick ops readout:

- Slot-map shows 4 of VivaReso's reserved workers are running at sustained 100% memory headroom; three additional jobs from another tenant (short-lived batch scoring job) spilled into adjacent nodes during the 08:30–08:50 window. We see KV-cache pressure contributing to serialization delays.
- We can free two slots by preempting the batch scoring jobs (they are not SLA-backed). Preemption will reduce queue depth by ~35% within 3–6 minutes.

Recommended immediate actions:
- Preempt noisy batch jobs now (Irene, please confirm when started).
- Flip route in the API layer for 20% of traffic to redwood-gpt-medium (quantized) as a canary — expect ~12–20% latency improvement for those calls. Marissa, please draft the brief.

If preemption + canary don't reduce error rate to <0.5%, we should escalate for a short-term reserved burst (finance + procurement).

—Priyom Das
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (urgent) increased 5xx and latency from dedicated pool

I've initiated preemption of the identified batch jobs at 10:09 PT — jobs terminated and workers reclaiming resources now. Observability: queue depth falling, KPIs trending down.

Live metrics (10:12 PT):
- Occupancy: 84%
- Median latency: down from 520ms to 210ms
- 5xx rate: down from 2.1% to 0.8% (still elevated)

Two follow-ups:
1) We need a short-term traffic policy to route non-critical inference to the smaller model until the customer's peak settles (20–30 minutes).
2) Marissa / Sales: customer will likely request credits for the outage window; please prepare a proposal pre-approved by Finance/RevOps.

—Irene Choi
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: ViraReso — operational update and credit path proposal

Aisha — apologies again for the disruption this morning and thank you for the patience. Short summary and commercial path: 

What we did:
- Identified noisy batch spillover and preempted non-SLA jobs at 10:09 PT.
- Implemented a 20% canary to redwood-gpt-medium while we monitored stabilization.
- Observability shows 5xxs returned to baseline by 10:25 PT and latency normalized across your reserved pool by 10:40 PT.

Commercial proposal (for your review):
- We will issue a one-time service credit equivalent to 6 hours of your committed reservation (applied as account credit) to cover conversion impact during the window.
- If this event repeats within 30 days, we'll open a dedicated capacity review with a recommended +20% reserved headroom at a discounted rate for the first 3 months.

Next operational items:
- Post-mortem draft (ops) due EOD tomorrow.
- Follow-up call to review root cause and longer-term mitigations: propose Wed 2028-09-06 10:00 PT. Please confirm availability.

Thanks — we own remediation and commercial make-good.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
